newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says ID system not prelude to martial law.
newsitem.headline: Manila says ID system not prelude to martial law.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos on Wednesday dismissed as baseless fears that his order creating a national identification system was a prelude to martial law.
"That is a wild opinion without any basis in fact," Ramos told his weekly news conference after Cardinal Jaime Sin, the outspoken Archbishop of Manila, accused him of being authoritarian.

"The mere fact that we are here discussing this openly, the mere fact that media have been allowed to discuss this openly, the mere fact that Congress has ... even threatened to impeach (me) is the proof itself of how far, far away we are from a martial law situation. Not under this presidency anyway," Ramos said.
Sin, the head of the country's largest diocese, said on Tuesday it was immoral for Ramos to implement a national ID system without popular consent.

Opposition politicians have said the system could be used to monitor political activities, that it was reminiscent of late president Ferdinand Marcos's efforts to curb dissent, and warned Ramos could be impeached if he did not withdraw his order.
Marcos ruled the country for 20 years, 14 with martial law powers, until he was ousted in a 1986 popular revolt.

Officials have said a computerised ID system whereby cards issued to citizens by state pension funds would carry reference numbers assigned to them for life would make it easier for people to transact business with the government and minimise fraud.
"That's all there is to it ... (its) very simple," Ramos said.
